title: The New Covenant
definition: The New Covenant is God's promised covenant fulfilled in Christ, bringing forgiveness, new hearts, and the gift of the Spirit.
summary: The New Covenant is God's promised saving arrangement in Christ, marked by forgiveness, new hearts, and the Spirit's work.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the mediator of the New Covenant, sealed by His blood.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The New Covenant is God's promised saving arrangement fulfilled in Christ, bringing forgiveness, a changed heart, and the gift of the Spirit. Scripture presents it as deeper than external religion because God writes His law upon His people's hearts.

This covenant does not lower God's holiness. It provides the mercy and inward renewal sinners need in order to know and follow the Lord.

Jesus establishes the New Covenant in His blood. At the Lord's Table and in the Gospel, believers remember that forgiveness and transformation come through Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because religion can become external while the heart remains unchanged. The New Covenant gives hope that God not only forgives sin but also renews His people from within.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God to shape your heart, not merely your outward habits. Treasure the blood of Christ, depend on the Spirit, and teach obedience as the fruit of New Covenant grace.
